Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 43, verses 3–4:

Ibn ʿAbbas said: "In the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), which is with Us."

Muqatil said: "Its copy is in the source of the Book, which is the Preserved Tablet. The Mother of the Book (Umm al-Kitab) is the source of the Book, and the mother of everything is its origin."

The Qur'an, God wrote it in the Preserved Tablet before He created the heavens and the earth, as the Exalted said: ﴿Nay, but it is a glorious Qur'an, in a Preserved Tablet.﴾

The Companions, the Successors, and all the People of the Sunnah and Hadith agreed that everything that will happen until the Day of Resurrection is written in the Mother of the Book.

The Qur'an has shown that the Lord, exalted is He, wrote in the Mother of the Book what He would do and what He would say, so He wrote His acts and His speech in the Tablet.

So ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab﴾ is in the Preserved Tablet before Abu Lahab existed.

As for His saying ﴿with Us (ladayna)﴾, it is permissible that it be connected to ﴿the Mother of the Book﴾, meaning that it is in the Book which is with Us.

This is the choice of Ibn ʿAbbas.

It is also permissible that it be connected to the predicate, that it is ﴿exalted, full of wisdom (ʿaliyyun hakim)﴾ with Us, unlike how it is with those who deny it.

That is, even if you deny it and disbelieve in it, it is with Us in the utmost of elevation, nobility, and firmness.

(Section)

Then consider the profound wisdom in God, glorified is He, giving the beasts of cattle hearing and sight, so that they can be used for their benefits and man's benefit from them is complete; for if they were blind or deaf, man would not be able to benefit from them.

Then He took away from them intellect, despite the great size of their bodies, which are for man, so that his subjugation of them is complete: he leads them and directs them wherever he wishes.

Had they been given intellect despite the great size of their bodies, they would have refused his obedience, resisted him, and would not have been subjugated to him. So they were given the discernment and perception by which their own welfare is accomplished, and the welfare of others from them for him; and they were deprived of the mind and reason by which man is distinguished over them, and so that the excellence of discernment and distinction may also appear.

Then consider how He led them and made them docile despite the greatness of their bodies, and he would not have been able to manage them were it not for His subjugation. God, Exalted, says: ﴿And He created for you of the ships and the cattle that which you ride, so that you may sit upon their backs, then remember the blessing of your Lord when you are seated upon them, and say: Glory be to Him who has subjected these to us, and we could not have subdued them by ourselves﴾

That is, capable and controlling.

And God, Exalted, says: ﴿Do they not see that We created for them, of what Our hands have made, cattle, and they are masters of them? And We made them subservient to them, so some of them are for riding and some of them they eat﴾

So you see the camel, despite its great size, led by a small child, docile and submissive; if it were let loose upon him, it would flatten him to the ground and tear him apart limb from limb. So ask the one who denies (the Creator): who subdued it, subjected it, and led it despite its strength, to a weak human, one of the weakest of creatures? That subjugation freed the human species for the interests of their livelihood and their hereafter. For if he had to perform the labors and burdens that animals perform, it would have occupied him from many tasks, since in place of one camel he would need several people to carry its loads and its burden, and they would be unable to do so. That would drain their time and divert them from their interests. So they were aided by these animals, along with the many benefits they have in them, which none can count except God: food, drink, medicine, clothing, goods, tools, vessels, riding, plowing, numerous other benefits, and beauty.

Then consider the profound wisdom in making the backs of the beasts flat, as if they were a roof upon pillars of legs, so that riding them is facilitated and the load rests upon them.

Then this was contradicted in the case of camels, so their backs were made humped and arched like a vault, because of the excellence of strength they were given and the greatness of what they carry, and vaults carry more than roofs do; so much so that it is said the arch of vaults was taken from the backs of camels.

And consider how, when God lengthened the camel's legs, He lengthened its neck, so that it can reach pasture while standing; for if its neck were short, it would not be possible for it to do so given its long legs. And so that the length of its neck would also balance the load on its back when it bears it, just as you see the length of the beam of a steelyard (al-qabbān, a balance scale); so much so that it is said the steelyard was only devised from the creation of the camel, from the length of its neck and the weight it carries. For this reason you see it stretch out its neck when it bears a load, as if balancing it.

The Exalted argues against those who attributed daughters to Him, saying that one of them does not accept daughters for himself, and when he is given the good news of a female child, grief and gloom overcome him, so much that darkness appears on his face. So if one of you is not pleased with females as daughters, how can you attribute them to Me?

As He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And they assign to Allah what they dislike.﴾ [al-Nahl: 62]

Then He mentioned the weakness of this sex which they attributed to Him, and that it is the lesser of the two sexes; therefore it needs adornment to be complete. And He mentioned their weakness in expression, saying: ﴿Is one who is brought up among ornaments, and who in dispute is not clear [in expression]?﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 18]

By mentioning their being brought up in ornaments, He indicated that they are deficient and so need an adornment with which to complete themselves, and that they are incapable of expressing their argument clearly at the time of dispute.

Along with this, in His saying ﴿Is one who is brought up among ornaments﴾ there is an allusion to the purpose for which ornaments were prescribed, namely adornment for the one who lies with them and has intercourse with them, and an allusion that they are not raised in war, combat and bravery. So He mentioned the ornament, which is a sign of weakness, incapacity and feebleness.

Ibn al-Qayyim said, may God have mercy on him, regarding the verses:

﴿And when Abraham said to his father and his people, "Indeed, I am free from what you worship, except He who created me, for indeed He will guide me." And he made it a word remaining among his descendants that they might return.﴾

That is: He made this allegiance to God, and disavowal of every object of worship other than Him, a word remaining among his descendants, which the prophets and their followers inherit from one another, generation after generation. It is the word "There is no deity but God" (lā ilāha illā Allāh), which the Imam of the Hanifs (Imam al-Hunafa') bequeathed to his followers until the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 43, verses 31–32:

Then He (subhanahu) denounced their choosing [for themselves] over Him, and informed them that this is not up to them, but rather up to the One who apportioned among them their means of livelihood, which include their provisions and the appointed terms of their lives. Likewise, it is He who distributes His bounty among the people of bounty according to His knowledge of the places of selection, and of who is fit for it from among those who are not fit. It is He who raised some of them above others in degrees, and apportioned among them their livelihoods and the degrees of preference. So He alone is the Apportioner of that, not anyone else. In the same way, in this verse He made clear that He alone creates and chooses, and that He (subhanahu) is most knowing of the places of His choosing, as the Exalted said: ﴿And when a sign comes to them, they say, "We will not believe until we are given the like of what was given to the messengers of Allah." Allah knows best where to place His message﴾ [al-An'am: 124].

That is: Allah knows best the place that is fit for His choosing, His honouring, and singling out for messengerhood and prophethood, to the exclusion of others.

(Section)

Asceticism (zuhd) has several divisions. There is asceticism regarding the forbidden (haram), which is an individual obligation (fard 'ayn).

There is asceticism regarding doubtful matters (shubuhat), and this depends on the levels of the doubt: if the doubt is strong, abandoning it approaches what is obligatory; if it is weak, it is recommended (mustahabb).

There is asceticism regarding superfluities (fudul).

There is asceticism regarding what does not concern a person (ma la ya'nihi) of speech, looking, questioning, meeting others, and other things.

There is asceticism regarding people, and asceticism regarding the self, to the extent that one's self becomes insignificant to him for the sake of God.

There is a comprehensive asceticism that includes all of these, which is asceticism regarding everything other than God, and regarding everything that preoccupies you from Him.

The best asceticism is concealing one's asceticism, and the most difficult is asceticism regarding one's own portions of worldly enjoyment (huzuz). The difference between asceticism (zuhd) and scrupulousness (wara') is that zuhd is leaving what does not benefit one in the Hereafter, while wara' is leaving what one fears will harm one in the Hereafter. A heart attached to desires has neither valid zuhd nor valid wara'.

Yahya ibn Mu'adh said: "I am amazed at three kinds of people:

A man who shows off his deed to a created being like himself, and leaves off doing it for God; a man who is stingy with his wealth while his Lord asks him to lend from it and he lends Him nothing; and a man who desires the companionship and affection of created beings while God calls him to His companionship and affection."

(Benefit)

One of the early scholars (al-salaf) said: "If you see God continuing His blessings upon you while you persist in His disobedience, then beware of Him, for it is a gradual drawing-in (istidraj) by which He draws you on."

And the Exalted has said: ﴿And were it not that mankind would be one community, We would have made for those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful silver ceilings for their houses and stairways by which they ascend, and doors for their houses and couches on which they recline, and adornment. But all of that would be nothing but the enjoyment of the worldly life. And the Hereafter with your Lord is for the righteous.﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 33–35].

Allah, glorified is He, informed that whoever is blinded to His remembrance, which is His Book that He sent down upon His Messenger, turns away from it, is blind to it, and whose insight is dimmed from understanding it, pondering it, and knowing what Allah intends by it, Allah appoints for him a devil as a punishment for his turning away from His Book. He is his companion who never leaves him, whether he is at rest or on the move, his master and his associate, and what an evil master and an evil associate he is.

؎Two who nursed at the breast of one mother shared,
beneath a jet-black, dark (night), an inseparable bond.

Then Allah, glorified is He, informed that the devil turns his companion and ally away from the path that leads to Allah and to His Garden, and this misguided one who is turned away thinks that he is on the path of guidance. Until, when the two companions come on the Day of Resurrection, one of them says to the other: ﴿Would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts! How wretched a companion!﴾ (You were) for me in this world; you led me astray.

(Benefit)

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it will not benefit you today, since you wronged, that you are in the punishment together﴾

Thus Allah, glorified is He, cut off their benefit from consoling one another in the punishment. For the calamities of this world, when they become general, become a source of solace, and some of those afflicted console one another, as al-Khansa said:

؎Were it not for the abundance of those weeping around me
over their brothers, I would have killed myself.

؎They do not weep like my brother, but I console myself for him through consolation.

This comfort that comes from consoling one another is absent among those who share the punishment on the Day of Resurrection.

(A Great Benefit)

When a servant begins his morning and evening with no concern but Allah alone, Allah, glorified is He, bears all his needs, takes from him every worry that troubles him, frees his heart for His love, his tongue for His remembrance, and his limbs for His obedience. But if he begins his morning and evening with the world as his concern, Allah burdens him with its worries, its griefs, and its miseries, and leaves him to himself, so that his heart is occupied with love of creatures instead of the love of Him, his tongue with their remembrance instead of His, and his limbs with serving them and their affairs instead of obeying Him. He toils like a wild beast in the service of others, like a bellows that puffs out its belly and squeezes its ribs, working for the benefit of others. Whoever turns away from the worship and obedience and love of Allah is afflicted with worship of a created being, with love for him and service to him. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And whoever is blinded to the remembrance of the Most Merciful, We appoint for him a devil, and he is to him a companion.﴾

Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah said: "You will not bring any well-known proverb of the Arabs except that I will bring it to you from the Qur'an."

Someone said to him: "Where in the Qur'an (is the saying) 'Give your brother a date; if he refuses, give him a coal'?" He said: "(It is) in His saying: ﴿And whoever is blinded to the remembrance of the Most Merciful, We appoint for him a devil﴾ (up to) the verse..."

(The companion says): "...away from the guidance after it had come to me, and you turned me away from the truth and led me astray until I was ruined. What a wretched companion you are to me today!"

When an afflicted person is joined by another in the same calamity, he gains through consoling one another a kind of lightening and solace, Allah, glorified is He, informed that this is neither present nor attained by those who share the punishment, and that the companion finds no rest nor the slightest joy in his companion's punishment being with him, even though worldly calamities, when they are general, become a source of solace. So Allah, glorified is He, denied the people of the Fire this degree of rest, saying: ﴿And it will not benefit you today, since you wronged, that you are in the punishment together﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 39]

He is his companion who never leaves him, whether he is at rest or on the move, his master and his associate, and what an evil master and an evil associate he is.

The meaning of their being asked is the asking of their nations about what the messengers brought them: whether in it there was that Allah had prescribed for them that a god other than Him be worshipped?

Al-Farra' said: The intended meaning is the asking of the People of the Torah and the Gospel, so that they inform him about their scriptures and their prophets.

Ibn Qutaybah said: The implied sense is: "Ask those whom We sent to them as messengers before you, and they are the People of the Book."

Ibn al-Anbari said: The implied sense is: "Ask those whom We sent before you."

In every case, the intended purpose is to affirm (taqrir) against the polytheists of Quraysh and others who denied prophethood and monotheism, and that Allah sent a messenger, or revealed a book, or forbade the worship of idols.

So the testimony of the People of the Book to this is a proof against them, and it is one of the signs of the truth of his prophethood (ﷺ), since he came with what his brothers, the messengers of Allah (subhanahu wa ta'ala) who preceded him, had brought. He was not an innovation among the messengers, nor did he come with the opposite of what they brought; rather, he reported the same things they had reported, without having witnessed them and without being contemporaneous with them. This is among the greatest signs of his truthfulness.

**Chapter: That women in Paradise are more numerous than men, and likewise they are more numerous in the Fire**

It is established in the two Sahihs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), from the narration of Ayyub ibn Muhammad ibn Sirin, who said: "They were either boasting or discussing: Are men or women more numerous in Paradise? Abu Hurayrah said: Did not Abu al-Qasim (ﷺ) say: 'The first group to enter Paradise will be in the form of the moon on the night of the full moon, and those after them will be in the light of a shining star in the sky. Each man among them will have two wives, and the marrow of their shins will be visible from behind the flesh.' And there is no unmarried person in Paradise. So if they are women of this world, then women in this world are more numerous than men. And if they are from the Hur al-'In (the wide-eyed houris), then it does not necessarily follow that they are more numerous in this world."

The apparent meaning is that they are from the Hur al-'In, as related by Imam Ahmad: Affan narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, Yunus narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said:

"For the men of Paradise there are two wives from the Hur al-'In, each of whom will have seventy garments, and the marrow of her shin will be seen from behind her garments."

If it is said: How do you reconcile this hadith with the hadith of Jabir, agreed upon (by al-Bukhari and Muslim): "I attended the Eid with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He prayed before delivering the khutbah, without adhan or iqamah. Then he delivered the khutbah after the prayer, admonishing the people and reminding them. Then he went to the women and admonished them, and Bilal was with him, and he reminded them and commanded them to give charity. So the woman began to throw her ring and her earring, and the like. The Prophet (ﷺ) then commanded Bilal, and he gathered what was there. He said: 'Indeed, among you there are those who will be in Paradise...' a little (in number). A woman said: 'O Messenger of Allah, why?' He said: 'Because you curse frequently and are ungrateful to your spouses.'"

And in another hadith: "The fewest inhabitants of Paradise are women."

It is said: This indicates that they are more numerous in Paradise only because of the houris who were created in Paradise, and the fewest of its inhabitants are the women of this world. So the women of this world are the fewest of the people of Paradise and the most numerous of the people of the Fire.

As for their being the most numerous of the people of the Fire, al-Bukhari related in his Sahih from the narration of Imran ibn Husayn, who said: "It has reached me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

'I looked into the Fire and saw that most of its inhabitants were women. I looked into Paradise and saw that most of its inhabitants were the poor.'"

In Sahih Muslim, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"I looked into Paradise and saw that most of its inhabitants were the poor, and I looked into the Fire and saw that most of its inhabitants were women."

Imam Ahmad related with a sound chain from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"I looked into the Fire and saw that most of its inhabitants were women, and I looked into Paradise and saw that most of its inhabitants were the poor."

In the Musnad also, from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"I looked into Paradise and saw that most of its inhabitants were the poor, and I looked into the Fire and saw that most of its inhabitants were the rich and the women."

In the Sahih, from the hadith of Ibn Umar, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said:

"O assembly of women, give charity and increase your seeking of forgiveness, for I have seen that you are the most numerous of the people of the Fire." A woman among them, a sturdy-cheeked one, said: "And why, O Messenger of Allah, are we the most numerous of the people of the Fire?"

He said: "You curse frequently and are ungrateful to your spouses. I have not seen anyone more deficient in intellect and religion who overcomes a person of understanding more than you."

She said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the deficiency in intellect and religion?"

He said: "As for the deficiency in intellect, the testimony of two women equals the testimony of one man; this is the deficiency in intellect. And a woman stays for days without praying and without fasting; this is the deficiency in religion."

As for their being the fewest of the people of Paradise, it is the report of Muslim (in his Sahih, reporting alone) from Mutarrif ibn Abdullah, that he had two wives. He came from one of them, and the other said: "You have come from so-and-so's place." He said: "I came from Imran ibn Husayn, who told us that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

'The fewest inhabitants of Paradise are women.'"

If it is said: What will you do with the hadith that Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili related: Amr ibn al-Dahhak ibn Makhlad narrated to us, Abu Asim al-Dahhak ibn Makhlad narrated to us, Abu Rafi' Isma'il ibn Rafi' narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from a man of the Ansar, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, while he was among a group of his companions, and he mentioned a long hadith, in which:

"A man among them will enter upon seventy-two wives created by Allah, the Exalted, and two from the children of Adam, who have merit over those whom Allah created, by their worship of Allah in this world..."

And he mentioned the hadith.

It is said: This is a portion of the long hadith of the Trumpet (al-Sur), and it is not known except through Isma'il ibn Rafi'. Ahmad and Yahya and a group have criticized him, and al-Daraqutni and others said he is "abandoned in hadith" (matruk al-hadith), and Ibn Adi said: "His hadiths are all open to objection (mimma fihi nazar)."

As for al-Bukhari, he said about him what al-Tirmidhi related from him: "I heard Muhammad (al-Bukhari) say about him: He is trustworthy, close to being sound in hadith (thiqah muqarib al-hadith)."

I say: But if he narrates such a thing that contradicts the sound hadiths, his narration is not to be considered. Moreover, the man from whom al-Qurazi narrated is not known to us.

Ahmad has narrated from him in his Musnad, from the hadith of Umarah ibn Khuzaymah ibn Thabit, who said: "We were with Amr ibn al-As on a pilgrimage or a lesser pilgrimage, until when we were at Marr al-Zahran, there was a woman in her litter. He turned aside and entered the ravine, and we entered with him. He said: 'We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in this place, and suddenly we saw many crows, among them a crow that was a'sam (white-winged), red in beak and legs.' Then the Messenger of Allah said:

'None of the women will enter Paradise except like this crow among these crows.'"

Al-A'sam among crows is one that has a white feather in its wing.

Al-Jawhari said: It is said of this, like their saying: "Al-Ablaq al-'Aqub" (the piebald raven) and "Bayd al-Anuq" (the eggs of the anuq bird), for everything whose existence is rare.

In al-Nihayah: "The a'sam crow is the one with two white wings."

It is also said: "The white-legged one," meaning that few of the women will enter Paradise, because this description is rare and scarce among crows.

And in another hadith: "The righteous woman is like the a'sam crow."

It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the a'sam crow?" He said: "The one of whose one leg is white."

And in another hadith: "Aisha among women is like the a'sam crow among crows."

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 43, verse 71:

It is said: "They will be served with seventy platters (ṣiḥāf) of gold, each platter containing a flavour different from the others."

Ṣiḥāf is the plural of ṣaḥfah (platter).

Al-Kalbi said: "Bowls of gold." Al-Layth said: "The ṣaḥfah is a broad, flat, wide dish. Its plural is ṣiḥāf."

Al-A'sha said:

"And the bowls (makākīk) and platters (ṣiḥāf) of silver, and the swift mounts beneath the riders."

As for al-akwāb, it is the plural of kūb (cup). Al-Farrā' said: "The kūb is a round-headed vessel that has no handle." He recited al-'Adī:

"Reclining, its doors clapping, a servant moves about with cups upon it."

Abu 'Ubayd said: "al-akwāb are ewers (abārīq) that have no spouts."

Abu Ishaq said: "Its singular is kūb, a round vessel with no handle."

Ibn 'Abbas said: "They are ewers that have no ears (handles)."

Muqatil said: "They are round-headed vessels with no handles."

Al-Bukhari said in his Ṣaḥīḥ: "al-akwāb and al-abārīq are those that have spouts."

And Allah the Exalted says: ﴿There will go around among them youths made eternal, with cups, and ewers, and a cup from a flowing spring﴾.

(Benefit)

Imam Ahmad said of Muhammad ibn Ishaq: "He is a transmitter whose narrations are sought after." Allah the Exalted has said about Paradise: ﴿And therein is whatever the souls desire and whatever the eyes delight in﴾.

This encompasses everything the souls desire: food, drink, what is heard, what is seen, and other things.

(Section: On Cultivation in Paradise)

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And therein is whatever the souls desire and whatever the eyes delight in, and you therein will abide forever﴾.

It is narrated from Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet ﷺ was once speaking, and with him was a man from the desert dwellers: "A man from the people of Paradise asked his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, for permission to cultivate.

He said to him: 'Are you not in what you desire?'

He said: 'Yes, but I love to cultivate.' So he hurried, sowed the seed, and it sprouted, grew, matured, and was harvested, piling up like mountains. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Take it, O son of Adam, for nothing satisfies you.'

The Bedouin said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we only find this among the Quraysh or the Ansar, for they are people of cultivation; as for us, we are not people of cultivation.' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughed."

Related by al-Bukhari in the Book of Tawhid, in the chapter on the Lord's speech with the people of Paradise, and he also cited it elsewhere.

This indicates that there is cultivation in Paradise, and that the seed is from it.

It is better that the land be filled with trees and crops.

If it is asked: how did this man ask his Lord for permission to cultivate, when He informed him that he was content without it?

It is said: perhaps he asked for permission to cultivate with his own hands, working it himself, and he was in no need of it, for he had been relieved of its burden.

I know of no mention of cultivation in Paradise except in this hadith. And Allah knows best.

Ibrahim ibn al-Hakam narrated from his father, from 'Ikrimah, who said: "While a man was in Paradise, he said to himself: 'If only Allah would permit me, I would cultivate.' Then, without his knowing, the angels were at his doors, saying: 'Peace be upon you. Your Lord says to you: you wished for something within yourself, and He has known it. Allah has sent with us the seed.' He says: 'Sow,' and it grows like mountains. Then the Lord, from above His Throne, says: 'Eat, O son of Adam, for the son of Adam is never satisfied.'"

And Allah knows best.

Know that God, glorified is He, made Paradise a house of recompense and reward, and He distributed its abodes among its people according to the degree of their deeds. On this basis He created it, glorified is He, because of the wisdom that His names and attributes necessitate. Paradise has degrees, some above others, and between the two degrees is as much as between the heaven and the earth, as in the authentic report from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, that he said: "Paradise has one hundred degrees; between each two degrees is as much as between the heaven and the earth." The wisdom of the Lord, glorified is He, requires that all these degrees be inhabited. They are inhabited, and disparity occurs among them, according to deeds, as more than one of the early generations (al-salaf) said: they are saved from the Fire by God's pardon and forgiveness, they enter Paradise by His bounty, grace and forgiveness, and they divide the abodes by their deeds. On this basis more than one scholar interpreted what has come affirming entry into Paradise by deeds, such as the words of the Exalted: ﴿And that is the Garden which you have been given as inheritance for what you used to do﴾

and His words, the Exalted: ﴿Enter the Garden for what you used to do﴾. They said: as for the negation of entering it by deeds, as in His saying:

"No one will enter Paradise by his deed." They said: "Not even you, O Messenger of God?" He said: "Not even I."

the intended meaning of this is the negation of the very act of entering. A better approach is to say that the "bi" (ba') which requires entry is other than the "bi" with which entry is negated. The one that requires entry is the ba' of causation (al-sababiyyah), indicating that deeds are a cause of entry, requiring it, just as other causes require their effects. The ba' with which entry is negated is the ba' of exchange and equivalence (al-mu'awadah wa'l-muqabalah), as in the saying "I bought this for that." So the Prophet informed that the entry into Paradise is not in exchange for anyone's deed, and that were it not for God, glorified is He, enveloping His servant with His mercy, He would not have admitted him to Paradise. Thus the servant's deed, however complete, does not by itself necessitate entry into Paradise, nor is it a price for it. For his deeds, even if they are performed in the manner God loves and is pleased with, do not equal or match the blessing of God which He bestowed upon him in the life of this world. Rather, were He to reckon with him, all his deeds would fall in return for a small part of His blessings, and the remaining blessings would still require gratitude. So if He punished him in this state, He would punish him while not being unjust to him; and if He showed him mercy, His mercy would be better for him than his deed.

As in the Sunan from the hadith of Zayd ibn Thabit, Hudhayfah and others, traced back (marfu') to the Prophet, that he said:

"If God were to punish the people of His heavens and the people of His earth, He would punish them while not being unjust to them; and if He were to show them mercy, His mercy would be better for them than their deeds."

The purpose is that His wisdom, glorified is He, required the creation of Paradise with degrees, some above others, its settlement with Adam and his descendants, and their placement in it according to their deeds. It follows from this that they are brought down to the abode of action and striving.

On this basis more than one scholar interpreted what has come affirming entry into Paradise by deeds, such as the words of the Exalted: ﴿And that is the Garden which you have been given as inheritance for what you used to do﴾

and His words, the Exalted: ﴿Enter the Garden for what you used to do﴾. They said: as for the negation of entering it by deeds, as in His saying:

"No one will enter Paradise by his deed." They said: "Not even you, O Messenger of God?" He said: "Not even I."

the intended meaning of this is the negation of the very act of entering. A better approach is to say that the "bi" (ba') which requires entry is other than the "bi" with which entry is negated. The one that requires entry is the ba' of causation (al-sababiyyah), indicating that deeds are a cause of entry, requiring it, just as other causes require their effects. The ba' with which entry is negated is the ba' of exchange and equivalence (al-mu'awadah wa'l-muqabalah), as in the saying "I bought this for that." So the Prophet informed that the entry into Paradise is not in exchange for anyone's deed, and that were it not for God, glorified is He, enveloping His servant with His mercy, He would not have admitted him to Paradise. Thus the servant's deed, however complete, does not by itself necessitate entry into Paradise, nor is it a price for it. For his deeds, even if they are performed in the manner God loves and is pleased with, do not equal or match the blessing of God which He bestowed upon him in the life of this world. Rather, were He to reckon with him, all his deeds would fall in return for a small part of His blessings, and the remaining blessings would still require gratitude. So if He punished him in this state, He would punish him while not being unjust to him; and if He showed him mercy, His mercy would be better for him than his deed.

As in the Sunan from the hadith of Zayd ibn Thabit, Hudhayfah and others, traced back (marfu') to the Prophet, that he said:

"If God were to punish the people of His heavens and the people of His earth, He would punish them while not being unjust to them; and if He were to show them mercy, His mercy would be better for them than their deeds."

The purpose is that His wisdom, glorified is He, required the creation of Paradise with degrees, some above others, its settlement with Adam and his descendants, and their placement in it according to their deeds. It follows from this that they are brought down to the abode of action and striving.

The acceptable witness with God is the one who bears witness with knowledge and sincerity, so he reports the truth, relying on his knowledge of it, as God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Except those who bear witness to the truth while they know﴾.

A person may report the truth by coincidence without knowing it, and he may know it yet not report it. So the acceptable witness with God is the one who reports it on the basis of knowledge.

And he said in (al-Turuq al-Hukmiyya):

God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And those they call upon besides Him have no power of intercession, except those who bear witness to the truth﴾.

That is, one who reports it and speaks of it from knowledge, and what is meant by it is monotheism (tawhid).
